messages:
Anna: Putting up a quick proposal: "cooperative preemption" for long-running telemetry reprocess jobs. Instead of killing or pausing, jobs will yield a small set of IO/CPU leases when live traffic needs them. Looking for implementation + console UX feedback.

Mike: yield = explain the primitive? a token/lease model or just dynamic cgroup throttling?

Anna: token leases + soft throttle. workers request X leases for a window; scheduler can revoke some leases and workers drop IO rate gracefully and checkpoint.

Sophia: host-level note: we can implement with cgroups + tc for network. leases map to io.weight and net qdisc classes. a tiny agent on the host mediates leases.

Raj: UX Q: how do customers see this? they need clear signals if backfill progress is being intentionally slowed.

Anna: console states proposal: RUNNING, YIELDED, QUEUED, PAUSED, DONE. show recent yield events timeline and a projected ETA that updates when yields happen. also per-job opt-in toggle.

Jordan: correctness: if a worker yields mid-shard, must be able to resume without double-counting. prefer checkpointing every N rows with idempotent write semantics.

Mike: ops: add safety fallback: if yields spike and some backfills never get any progress, after threshold move them to deprioritized queue and alert. set SLOs for resume latency.

Sophia: initial rollout: canary pool of hosts labelled telemetry-softpreempt=true. enable on low-priority backfills for 48-72h, monitor prod p95 and host io distribution.

Anna: metrics we need in telemetry: throttled_seconds, yield_count, avg_yield_latency_ms, resumed_from_checkpoint, host_io_percent_by_job. these are critical for debugging.

Mike: billing nuance: customers should not be charged for throttled_seconds as foreground compute, but we should record it for internal chargeback. add billing tag `yielded_seconds`.

Raj: console idea: when toggling soft-preempt on, show a small modal with estimated added time to completion, and a link to the host canary status. default = off; recommend on for adhoc historical recomputes.

Jordan: API sketch (REST/JSON):
```
POST /jobs
{
  "type": "recompute",
  "mode": "cooperative_preempt",
  "lease_count": 4,
  "checkpoint_rows": 10000
}
```
Response includes job_id and whether it was accepted into telemetry-softpreempt pool.

Mike: operator endpoint: POST /jobs/:id/force_kill and /jobs/:id/drain, with RBAC guards. also need a read-only /jobs/:id/leases for debugging.

Sophia: implementation risk: misconfigured qdisc/cgroup rules could still spike tail latencies. include a host-side watchdog that auto-relaxes rules if prod latency increases >10% p95.

Anna: integration with routing/quota: when yields happen we should surface in routing dashboard so model routing can avoid stale aggregates being read mid-backfill. maybe mark datasets as "under-recompute" for consistency windows.

Raj: good point. console data product page: badge "recompute in progress" and a freshness estimate. link to job details so customers can see which job is producing the recompute.

Jordan: checkpoint guarantees: each checkpoint write must be idempotent and include a monotonic shard offset + checksum. resume uses offset. unit tests should simulate revoked leases during commit to validate no duplication.

Mike: playbook for incidents: if a backfill causes host resource exhaustion despite yields -> 1) drain job via force_kill 2) revert to non-softpreempt hosts 3) roll back qdisc changes 4) notify customers flagged as affected.

replay-bot: backfill job bfill-901 started (job_id: bfill-901) on pool telemetry-canary-1.

Anna: next steps: I'll draft RFC with scheduler design, host agent contract, job API, telemetry keys, console mocks, and a rollout/canary plan. who wants to co-author?

Mike: I'll own scheduler + ops runbook.

Sophia: I'll own host agent + safety watchdog + canary plan.

Jordan: I'll own checkpoint semantics + tests.

Raj: I'll mock UX and write customer docs blurb + console copy.

Anna: Thanks team. opening RFC this afternoon. ping here for quick sync after draft is live. :thumbsup:
